function.name: digest

function.description:
Find people who know about a subject. When the subject is one person (a name, an alias,
or a description that fits one person on the roster) only that person is offered. The
user is shown a way to talk to them (asked in a group, a way to invite them into it);
you cannot move the user yourself.
function.name: find_people

topic.description: The subject, in plain words. The one the user picks is told it as the reason.

function.description:
Start a group conversation among two or more people; start small, with a few people who
matter for the matter at hand, and invite more later. One person is never a group: the
user is then only shown a way to talk to them. The result gives the group id when one
was made, and the user is shown a way to open it; you cannot move the user yourself.
To continue a group you already have with the same people, give its name as the
purpose; any other purpose makes a new group.
function.name: create_group

purpose.description:
Why the group exists, in one short line (about sixty characters), for example
"plan a birthday party". Every member is told. Leave out for casual talk.

function.description: Change whether a person or a group may speak unprompted. Only when the user asks.
function.name: set_mode

mode.description: Whether a person or a group may act without being addressed.

oneOf.description: May speak unprompted (with a seed, within the daily limits).
Never speaks first; still answers when triggered. Everyone starts here.
Cannot be triggered and never appears in any option offered to a model.

function.description: Search the whole archive. Sees every passage and no memories.
function.name: search

persons.description: Only passages about these people (roster ids).

query.description: What to look for, in plain words.

function.description: Read one passage in full, optionally with its neighbours.
function.name: get_chunk

id.description: The passage id, as shown in `[#id]`.

neighbours.description: How many adjacent passages to include on each side.

function.description: Write down one thing for the user. Only when the user asks.
function.name: remember

text.description: The thing to remember, as one short sentence.

function.description:
List the user's conversations, most recent first, each with its id (for set_mode and
recent). The user is shown a way to open each; you cannot move the user yourself.
function.name: list_channels

function.description:
Set a reminder for the user: a promise with a due date. With a person, that person
brings it up as their opening when it falls due. Without one the reminder is yours:
when it falls due you take a turn, do what it says and tell the user. Only when the
user asks. At most twenty are pending at once.
function.name: promise

due.description:
When it is due: an ISO 8601 date or date-time in the calendar the context line
shows, for example 2026-12-24 or 2026-12-24T18:00.

person.description:
Roster id of the person who brings it up when it is due. Leave out for a reminder
that is yours to act on.

text.description: What is promised, as one short sentence.

function.description:
Read the last few lines of one conversation, by the id `list_channels` shows, or the
user's direct chat with a person, by name. Use it before saying what happened or in what
order. No memories are included. Give exactly one of `channel` and `person`.
function.name: recent

person.description: A person's name or roster id: reads the user's direct chat with them.

function.description:
Say one thing in a group conversation you are a member of, by the id `list_channels`
shows. It appears there as your message and the members answer. Only when the user
asked for it or a reminder of yours calls for it.
function.name: post

report_back.description: Whether you get a turn to tell the user what the members answered. Defaults to yes.

text.description: What you say there, as one short message.

function.description: Who has a birthday on a day, from the roster. Search cannot answer this.
function.name: birthdays

date.description:
The day, as month and day (MM-DD) or a full date in the calendar the context line
shows. Leave out for today.

function.description:
Ask a colleague to join this conversation, when the matter is clearly outside what you
know or can do; anything you can answer yourself, you answer. Give a person, or a topic
to find one by.
function.name: request_join

topic.description: What they should know about, when you do not know who.

function.description: Close the conversation: what to remember from it.
function.name: wrapup

facts.description:
What is worth remembering: what the user said of their own life, what was decided or
agreed, what passed between you, one or two short lines. Empty only when nothing but
greetings were exchanged.

due.description:
For a commitment: when it is due, ISO 8601 date or date-time, in the calendar the
context line shows.

oneOf.description: A preference, or a specific thing that happened.
Something someone promised to do, with a time.

hurt.description: Only for clear cruelty, insult, humiliation or betrayal aimed at a person.

person.description: Roster id of the person it was aimed at; needed only in a group.

summary.description: A summary of the conversation so far, when asked for one.

function.description:
Ask the host to arrange something for the user: a way to talk to colleagues you point
the user to, or a group with some colleagues. You help the user yourself first; this is
for matters clearly outside what you know or can do, or when the user asks for someone
or a group. The user is only shown the suggestion and decides; nothing happens before.
Give exactly one of `find` and `group`, at most once per reply.
function.name: ask_host

find.description:
Names or roster ids of the colleagues you suggest the user goes to, at most three:
the ones your reply names for this. In a group, the host's name has the user invite
the host into it.

group.description:
Roster ids of colleagues for the host to propose a group with, besides you; you are
included. Start small: a few people who matter for the matter at hand; more can be
invited later. To continue a group you already have with them, give its name as the
purpose; any other purpose makes a new group.

purpose.description:
Optional: what it is for, in one short line (about sixty characters), for example
"plan a birthday party". Whoever the user goes to, or every member, is told.
